sentences.text: A steam whistle. A wooden tiller. And a mouse who loved to laugh.
The year was 1928 — one steamboat, one whistle, and a star was born.
Black and white, endless energy — pure joy, engineered frame by frame.
Ninety-five years later, the copyright clock ran out — and this classic Mickey belongs to everyone.
From theater shorts to the TV treehouse — a rounder, softer, sillier mouse.
Same ears. Same shoes. New playgrounds.
He has outlived trends, technologies, even time zones.
Because the trick was never the whistle. It was the giggle.
From steamboat to treehouse — nearly a century of oh boy!
Mickey Mouse — still riding the same river.
